editorial.description_en: Spring water coming out of rock — cold, clear, and blue-green rather than green.
editorial.description_ja: 岩から出る清水のような、青みのある緑。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.880, C 0.026, h 176.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 岩 (iwa, rock) + 清水 (shimizu, clear spring water). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Rock Spring" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 岩清水. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — tani-giri at ΔE00 4.3, shimo-ba at ΔE00 5.1, usu-rai at ΔE00 6.1. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.026 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
